title: Text strategies held in a UnaryOperator field

blocks.text: The page implements the Strategy pattern with an enum whose constants each receive a `UnaryOperator<String>` in their constructor: the behavior is a lambda passed as a constructor argument, not a method body.
The starter builds every constant with a placeholder operator. Replace each placeholder with the operator it names, and write `apply` and `applyAll`:

items: `UPPER_CASE`, `LOWER_CASE`: change case using `Locale.ROOT`, so the answer does not depend on the machine's default locale.
`CAPITALIZE`: the first character upper case and the rest lower case (`Locale.ROOT` again); the empty text stays empty.
`SNAKE_CASE`: trim, turn each run of whitespace into one `_`, lower case.
`String apply(String input)`: apply the constant's operator; a `null` input throws `IllegalArgumentException`.
`static String applyAll(String input, TextTransform... transforms)`: apply the transforms one after another, from left to right.

cases.says: Each constant applies the operator it was built with, and applyAll() chains several.
applyAll() applies the transforms in the order given, so TRIM then CAPITALIZE gives "Hello world".
CAPITALIZE of an empty text is the empty text.
SNAKE_CASE turns each run of whitespace into one underscore.
apply(null) throws IllegalArgumentException for every constant.
UPPER_CASE, LOWER_CASE, CAPITALIZE and SNAKE_CASE give the same answer under a Turkish default locale, because they map case with Locale.ROOT.

origin.section: Q1: How do you implement the Strategy pattern using parameterized enum constants?

concepts: A constant can take a lambda such as a UnaryOperator as a constructor argument and apply it, which implements the Strategy pattern.
